Assessment.source_text: So, what you've described to me, it sounds like you, you probably have got an infection in the chest

Assessment.content: Likely viral etiology given typical course.
Assessment.source_text: Yeah, and most of the time, these infections are caused by viruses, so they do normally settle by themselves.

Assessment.content: Diabetes increases risk of bacterial infection.
Assessment.source_text: With the diabetes you are a bit more likely to get a bacterial infection than if you didn't have the diabetes

Plan_of_Care.content: Obtain a thermometer and check temperature.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: it's definitely worth getting a thermometer and checking your temperature.

Plan_of_Care.content: Expect illness to settle in 1–2 weeks, though cough may persist longer.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: they do normally settle by themselves. But it can take, you know, a week or two, um, and you can persistently have the cough ongoing longer than that.

Plan_of_Care.content: May continue Lemsip but avoid taking other paracetamol-containing products at the same time.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: It's fine to carry on what you're doing at the moment, with the lemsip. I wouldn't take, and that, that contains paracetamol so don't take any other paracetamol containing products, um, with that at the same time.

Plan_of_Care.content: Avoid cough syrup during the day; if unable to sleep at night, a small amount is acceptable.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: the cough syrup isn't advisable in the daytime because it's best for your body if you just keep coughing. But if you're kept up all night and you can't sleep at all, then it, it's OK to have a little bit of cough syrup, just to settle that down.

Plan_of_Care.content: If not settling or temperature is ongoing/worsening, reassess and consider antibiotics.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Yeah, potentially. If it is, if it's not settling or the temperature's ongoing, getting worse, then we definitely need to talk to you again.

Plan_of_Care.content: Ensure regular diabetes and blood pressure checkups with the GP.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Well, if you make sure that you have the regular diabetes and blood pressure checkups that your GP has asked you for?

Follow_up_Information.content: Re-contact if persistent fever above 37.5–38°C, worsening cough, lots of phlegm, coughing up blood, nosebleeds, shortness of breath, or chest pain.

and if you feel like, if the temperature's ongoing, above thirty seven point five, thirty eight, um, and you keep spiking temperatures and that's not settling down, or your cough's getting worse, you're coughing up lots of nasty phlegm or you cough up any blood or get blood coming out your nose,
 um, or any shortness of breath, chest pain, then we certainly would need to speak to you again.
